newsitem.title: USA: NY's Bruno proposes $2 bln tax cut by 2001 - paper.
newsitem.headline: NY's Bruno proposes $2 bln tax cut by 2001 - paper.

text.p: New York Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno (R-Troy) proposed cutting business, energy and property taxes by $2.1 billion by the year 2001, the New York Times reported on Tuesday.

Bruno also said he expected the state to end fiscal year 1997 on March 31 with a $1 billion surplus, significantly more than the surplus of some $400 million projected by Gov George Pataki and Comptroller H. Carl McCall.
Bruno attributed the surplus to the state's economic rebound, which he said reflected cuts in state business and personal income taxes over the last three years, the paper said.

The Senate Republicans' tax plan, which the paper said was an aggressive effort to set the legislative agenda, calls for $700 million in property tax relief for schools by 2001. Districts that freeze property taxes would get more aid from the state to help cover rising costs. Additional aid could total as much as three precent above what districts were expected to get.

The gross receipts tax on utility companies would be reduced over the next four years, cutting $545 million from state revenues. Bruno said this would make it easier for electric companies to cut rates.

A number of smaller taxes on specific industries would be eliminated or reduced, such as sales taxes on car washes and food vending machines, excise taxes on liquor, container taxes on beer, petroleum taxes for railroads, income taxes on mutual funds, and estate taxes.
Under the Republicans' plan, tax revenues would be cut by $82 million in fiscal 1998, with the figure ballooning to $2.1 billion in 2001.

Bruno did not specify how the state would pay for the additional tax cuts. The state comptroller and fiscal monitors have said that even if New York has a surplus in fiscal 1997, it will face a $3 billion shortfall in fiscal 1998.
